subject: physics_2
question_text: What are thermal neutrons? What is their importance?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: the mean thermal energy at about 300 K is kT ≈ 0.025 eV, the standard value quoted for a thermal neutron. The capture cross-section of ²³⁵U for thermal neutrons is far larger than for fast neutrons, which is why a moderator is used. The book writes only "slow moving neutrons"; the energy figure is added here because it is the number the mark scheme uses.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. "Slow" plus the value 0.025 eV.
steps.why: A neutron is called thermal once repeated collisions in the moderator have brought its energy down to the thermal energy of the material it moves through — it is then in step with the temperature of the surroundings.
common_mistakes: Writing 0.025 MeV. Thermal energy is 0.025 eV, a million times smaller.
Calling them hot neutrons. "Thermal" here means slowed to room-temperature energy.

recall.must_convey: That thermal neutrons are slow neutrons with kinetic energy about 0.025 eV, in thermal equilibrium with their surroundings.

steps.memory_tip: Thermal = slowed to the temperature of the material around it.

steps.label: Importance

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name fission and the chain reaction.
steps.why: The capture cross-section of ²³⁵U rises steeply as the neutron slows, so a moderator is placed in the reactor for exactly this purpose.
common_mistakes: Saying fast neutrons are better for fission. It is the other way round for ²³⁵U.
Naming no isotope. The mark scheme expects ²³⁵U.

recall.must_convey: That thermal neutrons are captured readily by uranium-235 and cause fission, sustaining the chain reaction in a reactor.
accept: captured by uranium two thirty five

steps.memory_tip: Slow the neutron down and ²³⁵U catches it — that is the whole job of the moderator.

insider_note: Give the energy figure 0.025 eV as well as the word "slow"; the second mark is the link to fission in ²³⁵U.
